events.text:
**Recommendation:** Go to Grand Haven. Expect a below-average week at every port unless the wind shifts and brings an upwelling. Fish at dawn or dusk, casting glow spoons, or put out gizzard shad under a bobber.

**Ratings for this week (pier, salmon)**

| Port | Rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 1 (below average) | A few fish on gizzard shad or casting glow spoons (2025-09-10) |
| South Haven | 1 (below average) | A few kings and steelhead, mostly on cast spoons, but "overall, fishing was slow" (2025-09-10) |
| St. Joseph | 1 (low confidence) | No recent pier report, so this is a guess |
| Muskegon | 0 (slow) | "Pier anglers casting for salmon found the action slow" (2025-09-10) |

**What the reports say**
- The newest reports are 6 days old, dated 2025-09-10. Treat them as a guide, not as current conditions.
- **Grand Haven:** "Pier action was slow for anglers targeting salmon. … A few were caught on gizzard shad or while casting glow spoons." (Grand Haven, 2025-09-10)
  - The week before, pier anglers caught a few coho on glow spoons or bobbers with gizzard shad. (Grand Haven, 2025-09-03)
  - The pier was slow in the two weeks before that (2025-08-13, 2025-08-20) and did better in the 2025-08-27 report. Alewives and cast glow spoons caught salmon, but that report didn't rate the pier. (Grand Haven, 2025-08-27)
- **South Haven:** The 2025-09-10 report doesn't say whether the fish came from the pier. It says "most of the fish were caught by casting spoons." (South Haven, 2025-09-10)
  - The pier was "decent" (rated 2) on 2025-08-27, with coho and steelhead on spinners, spoons and shrimp under bobbers. (South Haven, 2025-08-27)
  - The Black River was a little slow, with a few salmon caught. (Black River, 2025-09-10)
- **St. Joseph:** The last pier report was 2025-08-06. Pier anglers caught steelhead and the occasional Chinook on shrimp (rated 1). (St. Joseph, 2025-08-06)
  - Boat fishing there was slow in the 2025-08-13 and 2025-08-20 reports. (St. Joseph, 2025-08-20)
  - Chinook were caught in the lower St. Joseph River and at Berrien Springs dam (rated 1). (St. Joseph River, 2025-09-10)
- **Muskegon:** Piers were slow in every report since early August. The only catch was "a few salmon" on cast glow spoons. (Muskegon, 2025-08-27)
  - Boats found fish far offshore, in 150–220 ft of water and 70–150 ft down. (Muskegon, 2025-09-10)

**Water and weather**
- The live conditions tool was unavailable. I only got last week's buoy averages: about 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, and 69 F at South Haven and St. Joseph. Those are measured.
- Surface temperatures changed by only about -2 to +1 F over the week. That is no sharp drop, so no sign of an upwelling.
- I have no wind forecast and no modeled cold-layer or pierhead temperatures. Check the wind yourself before you go.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension): north or east winds push warm surface water offshore and pull cold water up along the shore. That brings salmon toward pierheads.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52–58 F water. At 67–69 F on the surface, salmon will mostly sit deep and offshore, away from the piers.

**History for the same time of year (earlier seasons)**
- Pier fishing in mid-September was usually slow at all four ports. That was the pattern in 2022 and 2024 at Grand Haven, Muskegon and South Haven.
- The better pier weeks came with cold water.
  - Grand Haven pier anglers caught coho and a few Chinook on glow spoons the week of 2023-09-13, after a 10 F drop in surface temperature (Grand Haven, 2023-09-13).
  - St. Joseph had "good numbers of salmon" from the pier on spinners and spoons during a sharp drop the week of 2024-09-11 (St. Joseph, 2024-09-11).

**My read**
- I'd expect all four piers to stay slow while the water is this warm.
- I'd pick Grand Haven because it has the most consistent recent pier catches, including live or cut bait as well as lures.
- If you see a north or east wind and a sharp temperature drop, I'd move to St. Joseph first, then Grand Haven. Both have produced pier bites in past upwellings.
- I'd skip Muskegon.
